subtopics.title: Introduction and Definition of the Multiplier

questions.question: What is the correct definition of the multiplier effect?
options: An initial change in spending leads to a proportionately larger final change in national income.
An initial change in spending leads to a proportionately smaller final change in national income.
An initial change in spending leads to an equal final change in national income.
An initial change in spending leads to a change in the interest rate.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an injection into the circular flow?
options: Households saving money in a bank.

questions.question: Why is the final change in national income larger than the initial injection?
options: Because one initial injection creates a chain reaction of spending, generating multiple rounds of income.
Because the government prints more money to match the initial injection.
Because leakages increase when injections increase.
Because inflation increases the nominal value of national income.

subtopics.title: The Multiplier Formula and Marginal Propensities

questions.question: What does the Marginal Propensity to Consume (MPC) measure?
options: The proportion of any additional income that is spent on consumption.
The proportion of total income that is saved.
The proportion of total income that is spent on consumption.
The proportion of any additional income that is saved.
